reuse.why: Reuses budget mutation, spreadsheet, undo and average helpers, but copyPreviousMonth bypasses the new category selector and fixed-tag detection bypasses shared tag utilities.

duplication.why: Consolidates average actions but retains parallel eligibility implementations, repeated income guards and a custom implementation of tag matching.

placement.why: Budget selection and calculations remain in server budget actions, with method registration and undo wrapping in the existing application layer.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, related tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: The average consolidation helps, but maintaining eligibility across separate SQL and action-level implementations creates avoidable drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth/getBudgetData independently implement eligibility instead of using getMonthWideCategories; isFixedGroupNote implements tag matching instead of using shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts expresses hidden-category eligibility in SQL inside getMonthWideCategories and in TypeScript inside copyPreviousMonth, while template and fixed-group exclusions are also maintained along both paths.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideCategories takes includeHiddenCategories and conditionally constructs its hidden filter, but copyPreviousMonth bypasses that selector and separately implements the evolving eligibility rules.
